findings.evidence: Invoked as `/explain-changes-mental-model` (project install) or `/command-explain-changes-mental-model:explain-changes-mental-model` (this repository's plugin).
findings.fix: Delete the invocation sentence. The harness already handles slash-command discovery and naming, and the model never needs this to do the task. Keep the usage block only if it shows how arguments are classified.
Trim the usage block to the cases section 1 does not already make clear (`HEAD~3` as one commit, `#123`). Every other example repeats a numbered rule in section 1.

findings.evidence: Group files by purpose (not by directory), one group per reviewable idea.
findings.fix: Add a self-check before the output step: 'Before writing the report, compare the groups against `git diff --stat` (or the patch's file list). Every changed file appears in exactly one group, and every Depends on names a group that comes earlier in the review order. Fix the grouping and check again until both hold.' This turns the Process pattern into a checkpointed workflow.

Add a gotcha: '`git diff A..B` is the same as `git diff A B`, not log-range semantics. It includes changes made on A since the branches split, and those appear as reversed hunks. If the user means the changes on the branch only, use `A...B` and say which form you used.' Models routinely assume `..` in diff means what it means in `git log`.
argument-hint: [commit|branch|range|#PR|custom] (the hint is shown at invocation; without it users cannot see that the command supports the PR path in step 4)

findings.evidence: base is the first that exists of `main`, `master`, `origin/main`, `origin/master`, else ask the user for a base; then `git diff "<base>...<arg>" --no-color`.
findings.fix: Handle the branch that resolves to the base and the remote branch. If <arg> is itself the chosen base (for example `/explain-changes-mental-model main`), `main...main` is empty and the command wrongly reports 'No changes found'. In that case explain the tip commit as in step 7, or ask for a base. For a `refs/remotes/<arg>` branch, prefer the matching remote base (`origin/main`), because local `main` may be stale.
